record.paper_title: Some Open Problems on Functional Analysis and Function Theory
record.original_question: For metric spaces or Banach spaces X and Y and C >= 1, let B_C(X,Y) be the set of all α in (0,1] such that every (K,α)-Hölder map from a subset of X into Y extends to a (CK,α)-Hölder map on all of X, and let B_C^e(X,Y) = intersection over ε > 0 of B_{C+ε}(X,Y). Is B(X,Y) = union over C >= 1 of B_C(X,Y) always closed? Is B_C^e(X,Y) always closed? If B_C^e(X,Y) is closed, must B_C^e(X,Y) = B_C(X,Y), or at least must B_C^e(X,Y) be contained in B_C(X,Y)?

evidence.quote: In [12] and [9] the following notation was introduced: for C ≥ 1, BC(X, Y ) denotes the set of all α ∈ (0, 1] such that any (K, α)-H¨older function f from a subset of X into Y can be extended to a (CK, α)-H¨older function from X into Y .
Problem 5.2. Is B(X, Y ) always closed? Is BeC(X, Y ) def = T ε>0 BC+ε(X, Y ) always closed? If yes, is BeC(X, Y ) = BC(X, Y )? Or, more generally, is BeC(X, Y ) ⊆ BC(X, Y )?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be metric spaces (or Banach spaces). For $K>0$ and $\alpha\in(0,1]$, a map $f:A\to Y$ defined on a subset $A\subseteq X$ is called $(K,\alpha)$-Hölder if $d_Y(f(x),f(x'))\le K\,d_X(x,x')^{\alpha}$ for all $x,x'\in A$.

For $C\ge 1$, define
$$B_C(X,Y)=\{\alpha\in(0,1]:\text{every }(K,\alpha)\text{-Hölder map from any }A\subseteq X\text{ into }Y\text{ extends to a }(CK,\alpha)\text{-Hölder map }X\to Y\},$$
and set
$$B(X,Y)=\bigcup_{C\ge 1}B_C(X,Y),\qquad B_C^{e}(X,Y)=\bigcap_{\varepsilon>0}B_{C+\varepsilon}(X,Y).$$

Answer the following:

(a) Is $B(X,Y)$ always a closed subset of $(0,1]$?

(b) Is $B_C^{e}(X,Y)$ always a closed subset of $(0,1]$?

(c) Whenever $B_C^{e}(X,Y)$ is closed, must $B_C^{e}(X,Y)=B_C(X,Y)$, or at least $B_C^{e}(X,Y)\subseteq B_C(X,Y)$?

No authoritative source confirms the problem as solved, so its status appears unresolved.
